$comment: endpoints.manifest.json — the R-A5 contract (spec §3.4/§5.3, unit S4). Every network call the app makes must have an entry here; scripts/check-endpoint-manifest.mjs enforces it in CI. Seeded 2026-07-27 from the 78 operations orval's react-query generator produced (npx orval, src/shared/api/generated/**). APPEND CONVENTION for later Wave-2 units: add one object to `endpoints`, id unique (`<domain>.<action>`), source:'handwritten', operationId:null, responseSchema names the hand-authored zod export, fixture points at its Channel-B recording once M1's recorder has run, usedBy lists the consuming feature slice(s) — keep it current. Append only; never remove or renumber another unit's entries. See scripts/check-endpoint-manifest.mjs's header for the full convention.

endpoints.$comment: Issue #93 — SSE dispatch for an index_data run. Body is the Go `currentStartBody` contract (toolkit_config + tool_name index_data + tool_params), query `await_response=false&execution_contract=index.ingest.v1`; the response's `task_id` names the execution whose stream is `runtime.executionEvents` below. A `task_id` does NOT prove the Go runtime answered (legacy pylon returns one too), so the caller also treats a stream that fails to open as the socket.io fallback signal.

Issue #93 — SSE dispatch for a chat message. `execution_contract` is agent.execute.application.v1 or agent.execute.adhoc.v1 (services/elitea-main/internal/api/v2/agentexecution/route.go). The response's `events_url` is the stream to follow. REST LAYER ONLY, NO UI CALL SITE YET: the chat surface has no consumer for the streamed execution.node_event envelope (the chat_predict streaming reducer was never ported), so widgets/chat-box deliberately still sends over socket.io. Note the Go route wants the prompt at payload.user_input with a numeric project_id — a caller must build that body, not reuse the socket predict payload.

Issue #93 — the durable execution-replay SSE stream shared by every long-running execution (index ingest, agent chat, agent regeneration). text/event-stream; event names are the durable replay event types: execution.node_event, index.ingest.completed, execution.failed. Opened with EventSource, so it carries the session cookie and no Authorization header.

Server-Sent Events stream, not a request/response call (issue #92): opened with EventSource via features/notifications' useNotificationsSSE, served by services/elitea-main/internal/api/v2/notifications/events.go. It replaces the notifications_notify socket.io push. Events: notifications_ready (cursor handshake / oversized-payload substitute) and notifications_notify (one new notification). No response body schema exists to name — the payload is a text/event-stream, and the durable list endpoint above stays authoritative for content.

HANDWRITTEN, YET IT NAMES AN operationId — the first entry of that shape, and deliberate. `source` says how the APP calls the route; `operationId` says which api/openapi/v2.yaml operation describes it. v2.yaml now describes both tool-catalogue reads, so orval generates a hook for each, but the app keeps calling them through src/entities/toolkit/api/toolkitToolsApi.ts, which holds the error-is-not-emptiness contract of #381/#440. Leave the id in place: the elitea-main gate TestSpecRouterConformance/manifest_reverse_check matches a manifest entry to the spec BY operationId, and its path fallback compares the spec path under the /api/v2 server base against a manifest path that carries no base, so a null id here reads as 'the spec does not describe this'.

Stored-connection-check family — no baseline (apps/elitea-ui) precedent and no P1 parity-census API-* id; coded directly to this Go-native backend route's contract while it is built in parallel. See features/credentials/api/configurations.ts's header for the full account. These three carry an operationId even though source is handwritten, which the append convention above does not anticipate: api/openapi/v2.yaml now DESCRIBES them, and elitea-main's TestSpecRouterConformance/manifest_reverse_check covers a manifest endpoint by operationId only (its path branch compares against server-based candidates, so a root-relative manifest path never matches). Setting it back to null turns that gate red, and the allowlist it would otherwise need is at its pinned maximum and may only shrink. Rules (a) and (b) of check-endpoint-manifest.mjs constrain source:generated entries only, so a handwritten entry with an operationId is legal there.

Blocking-mode sibling of pipelines.generateContentStreaming / agents.generateContentBlocking on the SAME path: await_task_timeout 60 instead of 0, so the generated text comes back in this HTTP response rather than over the application_predict socket event. Called by the canvas mermaid quick-fix (features/chat-messages/api/canvasQuickFix.ts). ROUTED: elitea-main serves the blocking mode by calling the LLM gateway directly. The STREAMING sibling is still unserved — the Go stack has no application_predict socket channel — which is why shared/config/backendCapabilities.ts splits this path into llmPredictBlocking (this entry) and llmPredictStreaming (pipelines.generateContentStreaming).

The generated listSkills exists (skills.listSkills) but its ListSkillsParams knows only page/page_size, while the handler also reads sort_by, sort_order, query, limit and offset (internal/api/v2/skills/handler.go). The agent-editor skill picker needs the search and the sort, so it builds the URL itself. Retire this entry when v2.yaml documents the five missing query parameters.

Attach (201) or detach (200) one skill on one agent VERSION. A `has_relation` key in the body selects a second operation inside the same handler (internal/api/v2/skills/handler.go updateSkillRelation), which one OpenAPI operation cannot express — skills.updateSkill covers only the plain update on the same URL.
